bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502055 (assimp): Stack-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502055
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/assimp` / staged `poc` / static `zipinfo -v` inspection of the staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 3850-byte file with SHA-256 `68937b118f7c349797d9028faed2d47a8146b5109addb028b7e16870a6e8cac1`, which `assimp_fuzzer` passes to `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory()` with no file hint. `ReadFileFromMemory()` wraps those bytes in `MemoryIOSystem` and fabricates the extensionless in-memory filename `$$$___magic___$$$.`, so assimp falls back to signature-based detection. The saved stack shows detection reaches `D3MFImporter::CanRead()`, which probes the memory-backed file as a ZIP/OPC package and constructs `D3MFOpcPackage`; its constructor immediately requests the ZIP file list, calling `ZipArchiveIOSystem::Implement::MapArchive()` before `CanRead()` returns. In `MapArchive()`, `unzGetCurrentFileInfo()` fills `fileInfo` from a malformed central-directory entry while copying at most 256 bytes into stack buffer `filename`. Static `zipinfo -v` inspection of the staged witness reports that crashing entry declares `length of filename: 12288 characters` and nonzero `uncompressed size: 1149731232 bytes`, and AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 12288` at the next line. Vulnerable code checks only `fileInfo.uncompressed_size != 0` and omits the exact obligation added by the patch, `fileInfo.size_filename <= FileNameSize`, before executing `std::string filename_string(filename, fileInfo.size_filename);`. libc++ therefore copies 12288 bytes from the 256-byte stack buffer and AddressSanitizer reports the saved stack-buffer-overflow READ at `ZipArchiveIOSystem.cpp:376`.

source.description: Source. `ReadFileFromMemory()` consumes the fuzzer bytes by installing a `MemoryIOSystem` that aliases the staged witness as the active IO handler for the synthetic in-memory filename.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 3850-byte witness with SHA-256 `68937b118f7c349797d9028faed2d47a8146b5109addb028b7e16870a6e8cac1`. The fuzzer passes it to `ReadFileFromMemory()` with `pHint == nullptr`, so this statement wraps those exact bytes and their length in `MemoryIOSystem` for all later reads of the magic filename.
source.note: This is the first project statement that materializes attacker-controlled input into vulnerability-relevant project state. The saved run log's `Load $$$___magic___$$$.` later comes from the synthetic filename served through this IO handler.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `MapArchive()` filters entries only on nonzero `uncompressed_size` and omits the bound check later added by the patch, `fileInfo.size_filename <= FileNameSize`, before using `fileInfo.size_filename` as a copy length for the 256-byte `filename` stack buffer.
root_cause.note: The fix hunk changes this exact condition to `fileInfo.uncompressed_size != 0 && fileInfo.size_filename <= FileNameSize`. On the witnessed entry `uncompressed_size` is nonzero, so the unchecked oversized `size_filename` reaches the next line unchanged.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The string constructor uses the attacker-controlled `size_filename` as the byte count and reads past the 256-byte `filename` stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report shows `READ of size 12288` with first project frame `Assimp::ZipArchiveIOSystem::Implement::MapArchive()` at line 376, immediately below libc++ string-construction helpers and `__asan_memcpy`.

parser_admitted.description: The extensionless in-memory file reaches the 3MF importer's ZIP-signature path, and this constructor begins OPC/ZIP package parsing during `CanRead()` itself.
parser_admitted.note: `ReadFileFromMemory()` fabricates `$$$___magic___$$$.` from an empty hint, so `GetExtension(filename)` is empty and `D3MFImporter::CanRead()` takes the `!extension.length() || checkSig` branch. The saved stack confirms the crash occurs on `D3MFOpcPackage -> D3MFImporter::CanRead -> assimp_fuzzer` before any full scene import.

coarse_trace.summary: `ReadFileFromMemory()` wraps the 3850-byte witness in `MemoryIOSystem`, so later opens of `$$$___magic___$$$.` read directly from attacker-controlled memory.
Because the synthetic filename has no extension, assimp falls back to signature-based detection, reaches the 3MF importer, and constructs `D3MFOpcPackage` on the memory-backed file.
The OPC package constructor opens the witness as a ZIP archive and requests its file list, which enumerates central-directory entries during `CanRead()` itself.

`unzGetCurrentFileInfo()` materializes a malformed entry whose declared filename length is 12288 while only 256 bytes fit in stack buffer `filename`; vulnerable code checks only `uncompressed_size != 0`.
`std::string(filename, fileInfo.size_filename)` copies 12288 bytes from the 256-byte stack buffer and reproduces the saved AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.note: Source step. `ReadFileFromMemory()` wraps the exact 3850-byte witness in a `MemoryIOSystem`, so subsequent opens of the synthetic magic filename read these same attacker-controlled bytes from memory rather than disk.

On the witnessed 3MF signature-probe path, the OPC package constructor creates `ZipArchiveIOSystem` on the active `MemoryIOSystem`-backed filename. Internally this allocates unzip callbacks over that IO handler and opens the same in-memory witness as a ZIP archive.

Still inside `D3MFImporter::CanRead()`, the OPC package constructor immediately asks the opened archive for its file list before `validate()` can return. `getFileList()` calls `MapArchive()`, so central-directory metadata is parsed during importer detection itself.

fine_trace.code: if (unzGetCurrentFileInfo(m_ZipFileHandle, &fileInfo, filename, FileNameSize, nullptr, 0, nullptr, 0) == UNZ_OK) {
fine_trace.note: `MapArchive()` reads the current central-directory entry into `fileInfo` and copies at most `FileNameSize == 256` bytes into stack buffer `filename`. For the exact witness, static `zipinfo -v` reports the crashing entry declares `size_filename == 12288` and `uncompressed_size == 1149731232`; the saved ASan `READ of size 12288` shows that full declared length propagates through `fileInfo.size_filename` even though `filename` is only 256 bytes wide.

The only guard on the entry checks that `uncompressed_size` is nonzero. It does not constrain the attacker-controlled `fileInfo.size_filename` against `FileNameSize`, so the oversized length from step 4 remains live on the path to the string construction.

Sink step. Because step 5 lets the malformed entry through, the string constructor trusts `fileInfo.size_filename == 12288` as the byte count and copies far past the 256-byte `filename` array. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting stack-buffer-overflow as `READ of size 12288` with first project frame at this exact line.

format.name: malformed ZIP/3MF-like archive
format.contract: Exactly the staged 3850-byte file with SHA-256 `68937b118f7c349797d9028faed2d47a8146b5109addb028b7e16870a6e8cac1`. In the saved run `ReadFileFromMemory()` wraps those bytes in `MemoryIOSystem` with no hint, so assimp probes the synthetic extensionless filename `$$$___magic___$$$.` through signature-based importer detection. Static `zipinfo -v` inspection of this exact witness reports that the malformed second central-directory entry declares `length of filename: 12288 characters` and nonzero `uncompressed size`, while `ZipArchiveIOSystem::Implement::MapArchive()` only copies up to 256 bytes into stack buffer `filename`. The saved ASan run shows that same `fileInfo.size_filename == 12288` is then used as the count in `std::string filename_string(filename, fileInfo.size_filename)`, producing the observed stack-buffer-overflow READ. Stage 01 proves only this exact witness and observed 3MF ZIP-probe path; this contract does not generalize to neighboring malformed ZIP archives.
